name: Perplexity Spaces
description: Perplexity's project workspace feature: a Space is a persistent, named knowledge hub that combines live web search, uploaded files (and Enterprise connectors), per-space custom instructions, a default AI model, and an associated collection of research threads. It is the closest consumer analog to a Labmate lab/workspace — scope is defined by a curated source set (uploaded files + selected web/connectors) rather than a directory or repo. Spaces persist across sessions and support collaboration with role-based invites.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account required. Users sign in at perplexity.ai via Email (magic link/password), Google OAuth, or Apple. Each sign-in method creates a SEPARATE account (Google vs email are distinct identities; subscriptions cannot be merged/transferred) — a notable identity pitfall. Spaces are a paid-tier feature: restricted on the consumer free/Standard tier and unlocked on Pro ($20/mo, ~50 files per Space), Max, and Enterprise (up to 500 files per Space, more at higher tiers). Enterprise adds org SSO/SAML and admin-managed identity. People with a 'View' share link can often browse threads without an account, but contributing (adding threads/files) requires a Perplexity account (and typically Pro for advanced features). There is no anonymous/device-local mode for Spaces.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: First-class collaboration. A Space owner can invite collaborators by email or via a share link, with role-based access: Viewers (browse threads/read-only) vs Collaborators/Contributors (start new threads, continue existing ones, upload files, contribute). Owners/admins manage roles and access; a Space can be kept private or shared by link. Collaborators all use the same uploaded files/sources and per-space instructions, so a Space functions as a shared team knowledge hub. Enterprise adds org-wide file availability (uploaded files remain available to all org users in that Space until removed/updated by an admin) plus SOC 2, encryption, and admin controls. This is the closest consumer analog to a multi-user shared workspace/lab.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A Space is a fully virtual, account-scoped (or org-scoped) named project entity in Perplexity's cloud — NOT a directory, repo, or filesystem path. Each Space bundles: (1) a set of uploaded reference files (private to that Space), (2) a custom system prompt / per-space 'instructions', (3) a default AI model and Focus/web-source preferences, (4) optional collaborator access, and (5) all the threads run inside it. The workspace is defined by its bounded SOURCE SET (uploaded files + selected web/connector sources), not by a path. Spaces sit on top of the global Library: threads in a Space also appear in the Library but are additionally grouped under the Space's dedicated view.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Sessions are the threads (conversations) run inside a Space; each thread inherits that Space's uploaded files, instructions, and default model automatically. A user (or collaborators) can run/keep many threads within the same Space, and can also run threads OUTSIDE any Space (which live only in the global Library). So binding is two-level: a thread is scoped to a Space (workspace) when created in one, and every thread is also tied to the user's account and surfaced in the Library. Multiple threads per Space coexist; collaborators add their own threads to the shared Space. Threads outside a Space are global/account-level, not workspace-scoped.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Workspace (per-Space) context: uploaded files, per-space custom instructions, default model, and web-source/Focus preferences — applied automatically to every thread started in the Space. Session (per-thread) context: the running conversation and any thread-specific attachments. Account/global context: the broader Library, account-level settings, and any general profile/personalization. A key scoping control: per query/Space you can toggle whether answers draw from uploaded files only, the web only, or a blended response, and optionally filter to specific domains/source types — so the grounding scope is explicitly user-controllable. Files are private to each Space and not shared across Spaces.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: No on-disk config files (cloud product). 'Configuration' = the per-Space custom instructions (a system prompt set via 'Add Instructions'), the default model selection, and web-source/Focus toggles, all set in the Space settings UI. These per-space instructions apply to ALL threads in the Space (e.g. 'Focus on UK jurisdiction', 'Prefer peer-reviewed sources', 'Answer ELI5', 'Limit to last 24 months', fixed output structure). Precedence is effectively: per-Space instructions layered over Perplexity's base behavior, plus any account-level personalization; thread-level prompts then refine within a session. There is no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules-style file cascade and no documented byte cap on instructions. [uncertain] Exact interaction/precedence between account-level personalization and per-Space instructions is not formally documented.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: This is the defining feature. A Space is grounded by a BOUNDED, curated source set rather than a directory: uploaded files (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV; up to ~25 MB per file; ~50 files/Space on Pro, 500 on Enterprise Pro, up to ~5,000 at higher tiers) PLUS optional live web (toggleable, with domain/source-type filtering) PLUS Enterprise app connectors (Google Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Box, Dropbox, and knowledge/PM connectors like Notion, Linear, GitHub). Retrieval is RAG: Perplexity selects the relevant files and the most pertinent sections, and answers blend internal files + live web with in-line citations down to the exact page/sentence, with click-through to the source file. Web vs files vs blended is user-toggleable per query. Files are private to the Space. This maps directly to a NotebookLM-style notebook / Labmate corpus-defined workspace.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Cloud-managed, hosted by Perplexity. Spaces, their instructions, threads, and uploaded-file metadata persist server-side and survive across sessions (a Space is explicitly a permanent hub you return to, vs an ephemeral thread). For Enterprise file connectors, ingested files are downloaded/parsed and stored in dedicated AWS S3 buckets with vector embeddings in Vespa (Perplexity's vector/search engine) for RAG; the Google Drive connector offers Zero Data Retention mode (files not copied/stored beyond query-result citation snippets) and real-time permission enforcement, or optional local indexing/sync. State is mutable (files/instructions/threads added/removed). Enterprise: SOC 2, end-to-end encryption, point-in-time backups. [uncertain] The exact primary database for consumer thread/Space metadata is not publicly documented (S3 + Vespa are documented for ingested file content/embeddings).
persistence_and_history.session_history: Threads are stored server-side and browsable both inside the Space's dedicated view and in the global Library (a thread in a Space appears in both). Threads persist until deleted. History is portable via: (a) Perplexity's official GDPR/CCPA data-export request form (up to ~30-day fulfillment), and (b) third-party browser extensions (e.g. 'Perplexity to Notion - Batch Export') that can bulk-export entire Spaces threads to Notion/Markdown including sources, with scheduled auto-sync, processed locally in-browser. Structure is conversational threads with cited sources; users can download/open cited files from citations. [uncertain] The on-disk/serialized format of an individual thread (e.g. JSON schema) is not publicly documented.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Durable, user-authored layer = per-Space custom instructions + the uploaded file corpus (the Space's standing knowledge/persona), which apply to every thread automatically. Persistent project layer = the Space itself and its accumulated threads, which become a structured, searchable knowledge base over time. Ephemeral layer = the individual thread's conversation context. There is no documented automatic, silently-built cross-thread semantic 'memory profile' specific to Spaces — durable knowledge is explicitly curated (files you upload + instructions you write) rather than auto-generated, which is well-suited to a research/lab model. Free-tier file uploads carry a 30-day retention; Space-uploaded files in paid tiers persist with the Space.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Two retrieval surfaces. (1) RAG over the Space's source set: every thread can retrieve from the curated files (and web) with in-line citations — this is how prior uploaded knowledge is reused without copy-paste. (2) History/Library: threads are organized and findable within the Space view and the global Library (the free Standard tier even advertises 'access to search history'). Retrieval of past THREADS appears primarily navigational/organizational (browse Library / open Space) rather than a documented deep semantic search across all past conversations. [uncertain] Whether Perplexity offers full-text/semantic search ACROSS all of a user's past threads (versus RAG over uploaded sources + Library browsing/filtering) is not clearly documented.
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Spaces and their threads persist until explicitly deleted; a Space is the persistent counterpart to ephemeral one-off threads. Deletion: delete a Space (or page) via the '...' menu -> Delete, with a confirmation, and it cannot be undone; to remove uploaded files you delete the containing thread (files are kept ~30 days by default in the consumer flow). Self-serve data deletion is available, plus the formal privacy/export request. Enterprise applies ~30-day retention policies with point-in-time backups, configurable for Enterprise. Free-tier uploads expire after 30 days. There is no documented automatic TTL that expires an active Space itself — persistence is the point; cleanup is user/admin-driven.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Not a code-execution sandbox — Perplexity Spaces is a managed cloud research/answer engine, not a VM/container/worktree environment running user code. Isolation is logical/tenancy-based: each Space's uploaded files are private to that Space; Enterprise adds org-tenancy isolation, SOC 2, end-to-end encryption, and connector permission enforcement (the Google Drive connector dynamically respects native Drive ACLs and offers Zero Data Retention). Any computation (RAG retrieval, model inference, Labs/Pages generation) runs inside Perplexity's hosted runtime, not a user-controlled sandbox. Network/web access is a product feature (live web search), toggleable per query, not a security boundary the user manages. [uncertain] Per-tenant compute isolation details are not publicly specified beyond Enterprise compliance claims.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Not applicable in a filesystem/environment sense. There is no machine/env state, installed-package set, or snapshot to save/restore — the only persistent state is the Space's curated content: uploaded files, per-space instructions, model/source settings, and threads. 'Restoring' state means returning to the Space (which retains all of the above). No env-snapshot mechanism exists or is needed for this product class.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Cloud-only. Spaces are a hosted product (web and mobile/desktop apps backed by Perplexity's service); there is no local execution mode and no self-hosting. The only 'handoff' is data egress: official export or third-party Notion/Markdown export of threads, and Enterprise connectors that pull external content INTO a Space. No cloud<->local session migration.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: No managed multi-agent/worktree fanout in the user-facing Spaces product. Concurrency is simply multiple threads in a Space (by one user or several collaborators) and Perplexity's internal multi-step research (e.g. Deep Research / Labs running multi-source searches) within a single thread. There is no coordinator/sub-agent orchestration API exposed to users for Spaces, and no parallel-agent dashboard. Collaboration provides human parallelism (several people working threads in the same shared Space) rather than agent fanout. [uncertain] Internal parallelism of Perplexity's research pipeline is not user-controllable or documented as a fanout primitive.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Sessions (threads) are initiated through the Perplexity web app and the mobile/desktop apps, by opening a Space and asking a question (or creating a thread). Collaborators trigger via the shared Space link/invite. Enterprise connectors and the separate Perplexity Sonar API are distinct surfaces (the API is billed separately and is not the Spaces UI). There is no documented Slack/GitHub-issue/cron trigger for creating Space threads; entry is interactive via the apps.

implementation.implementation_stack: Proprietary, hosted by Perplexity. Known/observable characteristics: account auth via Email/Google OAuth/Apple (Enterprise SSO/SAML); cloud-managed persistence of Spaces, threads, per-space instructions, model/source settings, and file metadata. Ingested file content (Enterprise connectors / synced files) is parsed and stored in dedicated AWS S3 buckets with vector embeddings in Vespa for RAG; the Google Drive connector supports Zero Data Retention and dynamic permission enforcement. Retrieval is RAG blending uploaded files + live web with page/sentence-level in-line citations. Models are selectable per Space (e.g. Sonar family plus third-party GPT/Claude/Gemini). Connectors: Google Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive, Box, Dropbox, Notion, Linear, GitHub (Enterprise/Max). File caps ~25 MB/file, ~50 files/Space (Pro) up to 500 (Enterprise Pro) / ~5,000 (higher). Enterprise: SOC 2, end-to-end encryption, ~30-day retention with point-in-time backups. [uncertain] The primary database for consumer Space/thread metadata and the exact serialized thread format are not publicly documented.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Perplexity Spaces is the single closest consumer analog to a Labmate lab/workspace and validates several Labmate design choices. (1) Workspace = abstract, source-defined entity: a Space proves the 'workspace is a curated source set + instructions + thread collection', not a directory — directly supporting Labmate's abstract workspace_id (a MongoDB document holding instructions + source references) with threads linked by workspace_id. (2) Corpus grounding: the bounded-source-set RAG model (uploaded files + optional web/connectors, toggleable files-only/web-only/blended, citations to page/sentence) maps to Labmate retrieving over a per-workspace corpus in a vector store rather than re-injecting content each turn — and the Vespa-embeddings + S3-blob split is a concrete reference architecture (vector index + object storage). (3) Identity/collaboration: required account identity with email/OAuth and role-based invites (Viewer vs Contributor, owner-managed) maps to using the Discord connector identity as the user key and modeling workspace roles/permissions; org-tenancy isolation maps to multi-tenant workspace isolation. (4) Per-workspace instructions: the per-Space system prompt applied to ALL threads maps cleanly to workspace-scoped instructions in MongoDB applied to every LangGraph thread under that workspace_id, layered over global defaults. (5) Persistence/history layering: persistent Space + accumulated threads (durable) vs the live thread (ephemeral) maps to Labmate's MongoDB long-term session docs + Redis Streams active-session state (TTL) + LangGraph thread_id checkpointing; Library-vs-Space dual visibility maps to scoping history retrieval by workspace vs user. (6) Lifecycle/retention: 30-day file retention on free, user/admin-driven deletion, export-on-request, and Zero-Data-Retention connector mode suggest implementing per-workspace retention policy, self-serve deletion, an export API, and connector permission pass-through for any external-data integrations. (7) Connectors as source-ingestion: Drive/SharePoint/Notion/GitHub connectors that respect native ACLs are a model for how Labmate could let a workspace ingest external sources without copying beyond what is cited.
